Spain sits at 99%. The rest of Europe? Between 1% and 14%. This map shows how much of the continent can hold a conversation in Spanish, and the gaps tell a story.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ France leads outside the Iberian Peninsula at around 14%. Italy follows at 11%, and Portugal at 10%. Spanish is a Romance language like French, Italian and Portuguese, so the learning curve is gentler.
2/ Northern Europe is a different picture: the UK about 6%, Sweden 5%, Germany 4%, Finland 3%. Much of eastern and central Europe sits at just 1%.
3/ Zoom out and the picture flips. Spanish has roughly 519 million native speakers worldwide, second only to Mandarin, and it's official in 21 countries.
4/ Europe isn't where most of them are. The Americas hold the bulk, and about 13% of the US population speaks Spanish at home — roughly 42 million people.
5/ The only fully Spanish-speaking country in Africa is Equatorial Guinea, where the Instituto Cervantes estimates about 88% are fluent. A colonial-era legacy that outlasted the empire.
6/ Which European language do you wish you had learned? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
